summary: Tsering Dhundup Gonkatsang works in Tibetology and linguistics. He studied at Panjab University, Tibetan Children's Village, and the University of Glasgow, later serving as headmaster at Tibetan Children's Village and as Instructor in Tibetan at the University of Oxford from 2001.
Tsering Gyaltsen works in the fields of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He pursued his education at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University and studied under the traditional teacher Dudjom Rinpoche.

Tsering Shakya is a Tibetology and history scholar. He earned his BA, MPhil, and PhD from SOAS University of London, later serving there as a research fellow (1999–2002), teaching at Oxford, and joining the University of British Columbia around 2005.

Tsewang Gyurme is a scholar of Tibetology, history, and archaeology. He has served as president of the Tibet Academy of Social Sciences and was attested as president of the Tibetan Association for Sacred Studies in 2006.

Tsikey Chokling Rinpoche was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar who studied at the Young Lamas Home School. He served as master of Vajrayana ceremonies at Ka-Nying Shedrub Ling (~1976–2020) and was a board member of Rangjung Yeshe Shenpen.

Tsoknyi Rinpoche is a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar who studied at Khampagar Monastery and under several teachers, including Dilgo Khyentse and Nyoshul Khenpo Jamyang Dorje. He founded the Pundarika Foundation and held a post at Tergar Osel Ling Monastery.

Tsuguhito Takeuchi was a Tibetologist and linguist. He studied at Kyoto University, the University of Pennsylvania, and Indiana University (PhD, 1980–1994) under Christopher I. Beckwith, later serving as Professor of Linguistics at Kobe City University of Foreign Studies (~1995–2017).

Tsugunari Kubo was a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo and Rissho University. He served as president of Reiyukai (~1971–1993, ~2000–2013) and president of the International Institute for Buddhist Studies (~1996–2019).

Tsui Lan Liza Cheung is a scholar in Buddhist studies. She earned her Doctor of Philosophy degree at the University of Hong Kong (attested 2013), where she studied under doctoral supervisor K. L. Dhammajoti and teacher Toshiichi Endo.

Tsukasa Mizushima is a historian and Indologist who earned his undergraduate and doctorate degrees from the University of Tokyo. He held faculty posts at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies (1979–1995+) and was a professor at the University of Tokyo (1997–2018).

Tsultrim Allione works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. She studied under the 16th Karmapa, Chögyam Trungpa, and Namkhai Norbu, earned a master's degree at Antioch University, and founded Tara Mandala in 1993.

Tsultrim Gyatso is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He has served as a senior instructor at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies and was attested as Abbot of Drepung Gomang Dratsang in 1987.

Tsultrim Kelsang is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He held teaching posts at Otani University as a lecturer (attested 1984) and professor (attested 1999–2002), and was a visiting researcher at Ryukoku University in 2015.

Tsuneki Nishiwaki is a scholar of philosophy, Sinology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Tokyo University of Education (~1962–1970) and held academic posts at Doshisha University (~1978–1992) and Kyoto University, where he was a professor (~1992–2007).

Tsuruji Sahoda was an Indology and philosophy scholar. He studied at Kyoto University (~1921–1925) and subsequently held academic posts at Osaka University (~1949–1963) and Ritsumeikan University (~1963–1970).
Tsutomu Hatai was a scholar in the field of Indology. Attested in 1987, he succeeded Hiroshi Maruyama and served as president of the Ayurveda Research Society.
Tsutomu Horio is a scholar of philosophy and Buddhist studies. He studied under Keiji Nishitani and served as a professor at Otani University, attested in 1990.

Tsutomu Kubo was a philosophy scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo under Raphael von Koeber and earned a doctorate from Tohoku University. He held professorships at Tohoku University (1940–1946) and Toyo University (~1949–1954).

Tsuyoshi Yokoyama is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology. He pursued doctoral studies at Kyoto University (attested 2015–2017) and was attested as a special appointment researcher at the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies in 2017.

Tu Weiming is a scholar of philosophy, Sinology, and religious studies. He studied at Tunghai, Tokai, and Harvard universities (PhD 1968), held faculty posts at UC Berkeley and Harvard (1981–2010), and directed the Harvard-Yenching Institute (1996–2008).
